fixes.explanation: Nope, friend, that nickname is getting pulled. The LORD says, "For you will no longer be called tender or delicate." It comes right after she's told to sit on the ground without a throne. So the throne goes, and the soft names go with it.

Right, it's False. Babylon is told to "Go down and sit in the dust…" and then the LORD adds, "For you will no longer be called tender or delicate." I'd say a tender, delicate name and a seat in the dust don't go together.

Egypt doesn't show up anywhere in this chapter, friend. The line says, "Our Redeemer—the LORD of Hosts is His name—is the Holy One of Israel." The people named there are Israel. Babylon is the one being spoken to in this chapter.
No, friend, it's the opposite. The LORD says, "You showed them no mercy…" Letting them go early would be mercy, and that's not what the verse says. He says even the elderly got "…a most heavy yoke."
It's the opposite, friend. The LORD says, "even on the elderly you laid a most heavy yoke." So going easy on them isn't what the verse says. I think that's a heavy thing to hear.

False is right. The LORD says, "You did not take these things to heart or consider their outcome." She never stopped to think about where it was all heading. It's like hitting send on a text without rereading it.
That's the opposite of what she says. The LORD quotes her: "I am, and there is none besides me." Nobody greater is in her picture.

That isn't what the LORD quotes, friend. What she tells herself is, "I am, and there is none besides me." She also says, "I will never be a widow or know the loss of children." Neither line is about her days being numbered.
Wisdom is right. The LORD says, "Your wisdom and knowledge led you astray…" What she thought she knew steered her off course. It's like being so sure of your shortcut that you end up lost.

No request to repent shows up in these verses. The LORD says, "So take your stand with your spells and with your many sorceries…" He's telling her to bring out her spells and sorceries. I think it's a dare.

That's it. The LORD says, "…each one strays in his own direction; not one of them can save you." These are the folks she labored and traded with since her youth. So they scatter, each going his own way.
